elements.note: Report claims (odor, slurred speech, field tests) against the dashcam; arguable-probable-cause qualified immunity is the battleground.

defenses.name: Probable cause / arguable probable cause (qualified immunity)

Service and default disputes (Meza substitute service; AG not appearing)

damages.label: Arrest, five-day parole hold, forced blood draw, Santa Rita booking
damages.why_p: Liability turns on probable cause and qualified immunity; the dashcam is the lever.

damages.label: CDL wages Nov. 1, 2024 to Feb. 19, 2026 (68 wks × $2,334.60; shared with Matter 33, recover once)
damages.why_p: Causation runs through the DMV suspension; weeks after Feb. 19, 2026 excluded (mitigation, overlap with the background-check matters).

damages.label: Punitive damages for fabrication
damages.why_p: Fabrication supports malice, but qualified immunity and probable cause come first.

trigger.label: Clerk's default entered against Melano (or the AG appears for both officers)
trigger.note: Memo § 4: not in the settlement wave while service is being perfected. Nov. 1, 2026 is the CCP § 335.1 backstop for any state-law claims against the State / CHP (Bane Act; no qualified immunity) — the largest value lever on this matter.

repricing_events.if_favorable: Default against one officer: raise every p for Melano's share; the AG or the officer must engage.
repricing_events.if_unfavorable: Default refused or set aside: no change in merits value; service issue only.

repricing_events.event: State-law claims against the State / CHP added before Nov. 1, 2026 (verify the Gov. Code claim deadlines first)
repricing_events.if_favorable: A defendant with no qualified immunity and vicarious liability: raise arrest_distress and wages p materially.
repricing_events.if_unfavorable: Claims time-barred or not pursued: value stays with the individual officers.

repricing_events.if_favorable: Low or zero BAC: probable cause collapses; raise all p.
repricing_events.if_unfavorable: BAC over the limit: lower arrest_distress and wages sharply.
